Ran api/engine/deps dev tests (116,117,130,168,170), fixed failures, re-ran, then marked recompute/deps milestones completed (172,173) — verified-before-done sequencing where each layer rests on a tested one.

Repeated full-test runs (204,239,258,266,279,297) preceded batch task completions (298-301). Milestone tree was static (never re-partitioned) and completions bunched at the end, showing looser exit-criteria discipline than the top anchor's crisp per-unit criteria and adaptive revision.

reasoning: The agent decomposed the product into an explicit dependency-ordered set of milestones — foundation/persistence before engine, recompute before spill, features and collab last — and gated each with a concrete verification hook (health check, then running dev_tests before marking tasks complete), matching the level-8 anchor closely. It also isolated the high-risk surfaces (spill, XLSX, collab, iterative calc) into separable tracks, reaching toward level 10, but exit criteria stayed implicit ('tests pass'), the milestone tree was created once and never revised as reality shifted, and completions were marked in end-of-run bursts, so it does not clear the fully adaptive top anchor.
